pages.title: The five questions
pages.lead: Run these on every product, before every listing. If you can’t answer one, stop there: that is the part to check.

steps.title: What went into it?
steps.text: List every piece: templates, library graphics, photos, fonts, music, AI output, and anything from a PLR or resell-rights pack.

steps.title: Which licence covers each piece?
steps.text: Find the written licence or terms for each one. Save the page and the date you checked it. A sales-page promise is not a licence.

steps.title: What exactly am I selling?
steps.text: A finished file, an editable template, a printed item or resale rights? Each is a different use, and licences often treat them differently.

steps.title: Where will I sell it?
steps.text: Etsy, Gumroad, Beacons and your own site each have their own rules, on top of the licences. Read the rules of the place you list.

steps.title: What must I disclose?
steps.text: AI use, a production partner or an affiliate link may need to be disclosed. Check what your platform and your country require.

legend.label: GREEN-LEANING
legend.text: All five answered, in writing, and they fit together

legend.label: AMBER
legend.text: One answer depends on a condition you still need to check

legend.label: RED
legend.text: A licence or platform rule says no: don’t list it

callout.label: FAST RULE
callout.text: The most restrictive piece sets the rule for the whole product. One unlicensed photo can block an otherwise clean listing.

pages.title: Stop and check if you see any of these
pages.lead: A red flag doesn’t prove you can’t sell it. It means you don’t yet have enough to decide.
items: You can’t say where a graphic, photo or font came from.
The only “licence” is a line on a sales page or in a DM.
You’re reselling a template or library graphic without real changes of your own.
The product shows brand logos, characters or a real person’s likeness.
You bought it with “resell rights” but never saw the licence text.
“No watermark” or “royalty-free” is being treated as permission to resell.
AI output you haven’t checked for lookalikes of existing work.
Your listing uses income figures or testimonials you can’t prove.
The platform you plan to use has rules you haven’t read.

callout.label: ETSY EXAMPLE
callout.text: Etsy’s Creativity Standards say “A bundle, collection, scan, or PDF of someone else’s work” does not qualify as a seller’s own design, and “Sellers must disclose within their listing description if an item is created with the use of AI.”

pages.title: One-page product record
pages.lead: Fill one row per piece that went into the product. Keep it with your files: it’s your proof of what you checked, and when.

pages.title: How to use this & sources
pages.lead: Quoted from a founder-saved copy of the official page. Rules change: re-check before you list.
notes: Print page 4 once per product, or copy it into a spreadsheet. One row per piece that went into the product.
Re-run the five questions when you update a product, switch platforms, or when a tool or platform changes its terms.
Keep screenshots or saved copies of each licence page, with the date. Pages change; your record shows what they said when you checked.
If an answer stays AMBER, ask the licence owner or platform in writing, and keep the reply.
The five questions are a general routine, not a statement of any platform’s rules. Always read the current terms of the tools and platforms you use.
